html:
Zog I was the only king of Albania, ruling as prime minister and president from 1925 and as king from 1928 until the Italian invasion of 1939. He was born Ahmet Zogu in 1895 to a chieftain family of the Mat region.

He took power in 1924 with help from Yugoslavia and brought order to a country of feuding clans, disarming the highlands and building roads and schools. He survived dozens of plots and assassination attempts, including a shooting in Vienna in 1931. To pay for his state he relied on loans from Fascist Italy, which gained more and more control. When Mussolini invaded he fled with the gold reserve and never returned. He died in France in 1961, and his son Leka claimed the throne in exile.
